summary: The Ed25519 signature algorithm has been implemented in OpenSSH. This document updates the IANA registry of SSHFP public key algorithms by adding an algorithm number for Ed25519, so SSH host keys of that type can be published in DNS.

plainLanguage.summary: SSHFP records publish fingerprints of SSH server public keys in DNS. This RFC adds Ed25519 as a key algorithm that can be identified in those records.

subtitle: Adds an SSHFP algorithm number for Ed25519 public keys.

tldr.problem: The SSHFP public-key algorithm registry did not have an algorithm number for Ed25519.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7479 adds value 4 for Ed25519 and gives an example SSHFP record using a SHA-256 fingerprint.
tldr.outcome: The IANA registry now has an Ed25519 entry; secure SSHFP verification still depends on the relevant administrators and client behavior.

today: RFC 7479 is an Informational RFC. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Ed25519 in SSHFP Records
sections.content:
RFC 4255 defines the SSHFP DNS resource record, which can publish a fingerprint of an SSH server public key. Ed25519-SHA-512 had been implemented in OpenSSH, but the IANA registry did not yet include an algorithm number for Ed25519.

RFC 7479 updates the registry to add that number and describes how an Ed25519 public key can be represented in an SSHFP record.
sections.plainLanguage: An SSHFP record publishes a fingerprint for an SSH server key in DNS. This document adds an identifier for Ed25519 keys.

sections.title: Public Key and Fingerprint Encoding
sections.content:
The RFC describes an Ed25519 public key as a 32-octet value representing a 255-bit y-coordinate and a sign bit for the corresponding x-coordinate.

The example SSHFP record uses algorithm number 4 for Ed25519 and fingerprint type 2 for SHA-256. The resulting opaque octet string is placed as is in the RDATA fingerprint field.
sections.plainLanguage: The public key is encoded as 32 octets. In the example record, the fingerprint is calculated with SHA-256.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The security of using SSHFP to verify an SSH host key depends on the security policies of the SSH host administrator and DNS zone administrator, how the SSH implementation performs verification, and whether the client accesses DNS securely.

The RFC refers readers to RFC 4255 for the broader security discussion.
sections.plainLanguage: A fingerprint record helps only if administrators publish it securely and the client checks it correctly. The RFC points to RFC 4255 for more detail.

references.text: Schlyter, J. and W. Griffin, "Using DNS to Securely Publish Secure Shell (SSH) Key Fingerprints", RFC 4255, January 2006.
